$comment: CMS-0057-F acceptance scenario manifest — the machine-readable SOURCE OF TRUTH for scenario status. The acceptance suite validates its [Trait("Scenario",...)] against this file (see ScenarioManifestTests), and tools/Cms0057Evidence generates versioned evidence from it. Statuses are one of: PASSABLE, PARTIAL, GAP, N/A. 'replace' is Cloud Health Office product capability (Replace mode). 'augment' is external-core integration capability (per backend). Do not invent Facets/HealthEdge results until an integration exists.

capabilityDefinitions.PASSABLE: The repository's defined acceptance scenario is supported by the tested implementation. Not a CMS certification and not by itself production readiness for a specific payer deployment.
capabilityDefinitions.PARTIAL: Core of the scenario is implemented; some part is engagement or roadmap work.
capabilityDefinitions.GAP: Not implemented in the tested code; tracked so it is not silently claimed.
capabilityDefinitions.N/A: The scenario has no dependency on this backend/dimension.

scenarios.name: Drug exclusion from medical PA scope

replace.rationale: The CHO Replace-mode authorization workflow enforces benefit drug/service exclusions: a request for a plan-excluded drug (or the pharmacy service type, out of the CMS-0057-F medical scope) is recorded as a coded denial and persisted with audit history, rather than following the ordinary approvable path.

scenarios.name: Provider Access — attributed member data pull

qnxt.rationale: QNXT provider directory pull is per-engagement integration work; product path uses the CHO projection.

replace.rationale: CHO Replace mode implements inbound Payer-to-Payer respond: a dedicated application service (PayerToPayerExchangeService) deterministically matches the transitioning member within the tenant, enforces the member's authorization via a server-side consent gate (never a caller-supplied value; an Active consent whose purpose is explicitly PayerToPayerExchange — see P2P-03), and assembles a member-scoped FHIR export (Patient + Coverage + CARIN EOBs) from CHO-owned data with a 5-year lookback and an audit trail. Outbound initiation (P2P-02) and $member-match/concurrent coverage (P2P-04) are separate paths, implemented in their own scenarios.

Cloud Health Office Replace mode initiates the outbound exchange as the member’s new payer: a dedicated application service (PayerToPayerOutboundService) resolves the member and the prior-payer coverage context from CHO-owned data (tenant-scoped; overlapping coverages with the target payer refuse rather than guess), resolves the target payer through a trusted, tenant-scoped, fail-closed directory (IPayerToPayerEndpointResolver — a caller names a payer id, never a URL, and a non-HTTPS entry is rejected, so no caller-controlled request forgery), enforces the member’s Payer-to-Payer consent purpose server-side before anything leaves CHO, and again before the export (see P2P-03), calls the remote Patient/$member-match through a transport seam (IPayerToPayerRemoteClient), requests the member-data export ONLY after a single member resolves, and validates the returned FHIR Bundle for member consistency (single matched Patient; no foreign Patient reference) before stamping it with source-payer Provenance. Outcomes are structured (target payer not configured / not authorized / no match / ambiguous / remote unauthorized / remote unavailable / invalid response), recorded on a durable-shaped exchange record with an idempotency key so a retried transition resumes one exchange, and audited without demographics, payloads, endpoint URLs, or credentials. A validated package is then durably ingested (PayerToPayerPackageIngestionService): resources are classified against the types CHO's FHIR surface actually serves, intra-package references are normalized to CHO's imported identities, and every row is staged under a deterministic import key (tenant + member + source payer + type + source id) before a single-document ledger commit publishes it — so a replay does not duplicate history, two payers' records are never merged, and a failed ingestion leaves the member's record untouched rather than half-written. Imported data is stored apart from CHO's authoritative member/enrollment/claim stores, so a prior payer's Patient or Coverage can never become CHO-owned, and the exchange reaches Completed only after the commit lands. Resource types CHO does not serve (Condition, Observation, and the rest of the USCDI clinical set — the same gap that keeps PAT-02 PARTIAL) are named and counted on the exchange and preserved in an archived package rather than ingested or dropped. Imported data is not yet projected into CHO's FHIR read APIs; live payer onboarding (SMART Backend Services / UDAP client registration, mTLS) remains deployment integration behind the credential-provider seam.

qnxt.rationale: No external-core P2P integration: outbound initiation against a QNXT-backed deployment is not implemented.

replace.rationale: Payer-to-Payer authorization is a first-class consent purpose, enforced server-side in both directions. The consent registry carries an explicit purpose-of-use axis (ConsentPurposeOfUse: PayerToPayerExchange, ProviderAccess) orthogonal to the §164.508 instrument type, aligned with FHIR Consent.provision.purpose; a shared ConsentAuthorizationPolicy is the single answer both the inbound respond (PayerToPayerExchangeService) and the outbound initiation (PayerToPayerOutboundService) evaluate, so neither direction can drift more permissive. An exchange requires an Active consent FOR the Payer-to-Payer purpose that is in force at evaluation time: a Provider Access consent does not authorize it, a consent with no purpose recorded does not authorize it (records predating the axis default to Unspecified, so no history is silently reinterpreted), and Draft, Revoked, expired, and not-yet-effective records each deny with their own reason code. The period is applied by the policy rather than trusted from the stored status, so a lapsed authorization cannot be used in the window before the registry writes the transition. Consent is never accepted from a caller — no request type on either direction carries one — and an unreadable registry denies rather than defaulting open. Authorization is re-evaluated at each disclosure boundary: outbound checks before the $member-match (so an unauthorized member’s identity never leaves CHO) and again before the export, and a revocation landing between the two stops the data request. A retry re-asks the registry rather than inheriting the earlier decision. Each exchange and audit record carries the authorizing consent id and a structured reason code, so “what specifically allowed this disclosure?” is answerable from durable state without any consent content. The registry in consent-service is authoritative when configured; Demo mode serves the same purpose/status/period records through the same policy. Provider Access enforcement does not yet read the registry — CONSENT-01 stays PARTIAL for that reason.

Cloud Health Office Replace mode implements the FHIR Patient/$member-match operation as a dedicated application service (PayerToPayerMemberMatchService): it resolves a transitioning member across payer contexts within the tenant from normalized identity attributes, using a deterministic strong-vs-supporting policy (a strong identifier — member/subscriber id or SSN — or the family-name + birth-date pair, with any contradiction failing closed) so zero candidates yield no match, more than one yields ambiguous, and cross-tenant identities are never visible. Concurrent/overlapping coverage is selected deterministically by requested payer/subscriber context and effective date (overlaps without a discriminator refuse rather than guess). The resolved member/coverage context is consumable by the P2P-01 export path. The same resolved context is what the outbound initiation path (P2P-02) uses when interpreting a remote payer's match; Provider Access enforcement through the consent registry (CONSENT-01) remains PARTIAL.

scenarios.name: Patient Access — member claims / CARIN EOB

qnxt.rationale: QNXT claims read is per-engagement integration work; product path projects CHO claims to CARIN EOB.

replace.rationale: Demographics validate against US Core; broader USCDI clinical data lives in an external clinical store.
PA data is a recognized resource type; the >=1-year retention / 1-business-day freshness job is not implemented.
SMART discovery, scopes, and PKCE are served; the identity provider is configured per engagement.

One registry (consent-service) carries the opt-in/opt-out lifecycle and now distinguishes what each consent authorizes via an explicit purpose-of-use axis, on one aggregate and one state machine rather than separate stores per purpose. Payer-to-Payer authorization is enforced through it (P2P-03). It stays PARTIAL because the Provider Access READ PATH does not consult the registry: Provider Access is governed by attribution plus SMART scopes today, so the registry can express a Provider Access consent that nothing enforces. Closing this means wiring the Provider Access path to the same policy — it is deliberately NOT claimed on the back of the Payer-to-Payer work.

qnxt.rationale: Metrics over QNXT-owned authorization data are per-engagement integration work; product path derives from the persisted CHO authorization record. The full public-metrics extract job remains engagement work.
